title: Social Services Legislation Amendment (Workforce Incentive) Bill 2022
short_title: Social Services Legislation Amendment (Workforce Incentive) Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would let eligible age pensioners and veterans' payment recipients suspend their payments, rather than lose them through cancellation, when employment income prevents payment.
It would generally allow suspension for two years and extend pensioner concession card eligibility for working pensioners and eligible pensioner partners for up to two years.
The measures would also cover qualifying partners of disability support pensioners, with commencement on the first quarterly starting date following royal assent.
changes: Eligible recipients could restart pension payments during suspension by updating their details rather than lodging a fresh claim.
Age pension suspension would require employment performed in Australia and Australian residence when the suspension decision was made.
Some late notification cases could receive a suspension period of two years and 14 days.
The bill would provide suspension protection for partners after separation or the death of the other member of the couple.
summary.affected: Working pensioners and qualifying pensioner partners would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Trevor Evans
speeches.brief: The Social Services Legislation Amendment (Workforce Incentive) Bill 2022 was introduced to allow age pension, disability support pension, and veteran entitlement recipients to have their pension suspended for up to two years—rather than cancelled after 12 weeks—when they exceed the income limit, and to retain their Pensioner Concession Card for two years, with an abridged reapplication process, to encourage workforce participation and address labour shortages.
